items.title: Step 1
items.description:
In this workshop, you are going to build an artifact provenance auditor. You'll store museum artifacts in an object and write functions to look them up, tag them, move them between galleries, and summarize their history.

Each artifact is stored under its ID. Create an object named `collection` and add an entry to it. Set the key to `101` and the value to an object with a `title` of `"Golden Mask"` and a `category` of `"Ceremonial"`.

hints.text: You should declare a variable named `collection`.
`collection` should be an object.
`collection` should have one entry.
The artifact stored under `101` should be an object.
The artifact stored under `101` should have a `title` of `"Golden Mask"`.
The artifact stored under `101` should have a `category` of `"Ceremonial"`.

items.title: Step 2
items.description:
Every artifact has a person responsible for it.

Add a `curator` property to the artifact stored under the key `101`, and set its value to an object with an `id` of `201` and a `name` of `"Earl Sinclair"`.

hints.text: The artifact stored under `101` should have a `curator` property.
The `curator` should be an object.
The `curator` should have an `id` of `201`.
The `curator` should have a `name` of `"Earl Sinclair"`.

items.title: Step 3
items.description:
Each artifact also tracks where it has been, how it is described, and whether it is on display.

Add three more properties to the artifact stored under `101`:

- `locations`: an array holding two objects, `{ gallery: "Hall A", year: 2020 }` and `{ gallery: "Hall C", year: 2024 }`
- `tags`: an array holding the strings `"gold"` and `"egypt"`
- `onDisplay`: the boolean `true`

hints.text: The artifact's `locations` should be an array of the two given location objects.
The artifact's `tags` should be `["gold", "egypt"]`.
The artifact's `onDisplay` should be `true`.

items.title: Step 4
items.description:
The museum has more than one artifact on record. Add a second artifact to `collection` under the key `102`, following the same shape as the first.

Use these values:

```js
{
  title: "Bronze Tablet",
  category: "Inscription",
  curator: {
    id: 202,
    name: "Robert Sinclair",
  },
  locations: [{ gallery: "Archive Wing", year: 2019 }],
  tags: ["bronze", "writing"],
  onDisplay: false,
}
```

hints.text: `collection` should have two entries.
The artifact stored under `102` should match the described object.

items.title: Step 5
items.description:
Auditing starts with reading what is already on record. Since each artifact is stored under its ID, you can access one by putting that ID in square brackets, like `collection[101]`.

Call `console.log()` with `collection[101].title` to log the first artifact's title. Then, call `console.log()` with `collection[101].curator.name` to log its curator's name.

hints.text: You should log the first artifact's `title` to the console.
You should log the first artifact's curator `name` to the console.
You should log the `title` first, and the curator `name` second.

items.title: Step 6
items.description:
Staff look up artifacts dozens of times a day, so your auditor needs a reusable lookup. The square brackets can also take a variable, so `collection[id]` returns whichever artifact that `id` refers to.

Create a function named `getArtifactTitle` that takes an `id` parameter. Use `collection[id]` to get the artifact, store it in a variable named `artifact`, and return `artifact.title`.

hints.text: You should have a function named `getArtifactTitle` with a parameter named `id`.
You should assign `collection[id]` to a variable named `artifact`.
`getArtifactTitle` should return `artifact.title`.
`getArtifactTitle(101)` should return `"Golden Mask"`.
`getArtifactTitle(102)` should return `"Bronze Tablet"`.

items.title: Step 7
items.description:
Sometimes staff will ask for an artifact the museum does not have. If no artifact is stored under that `id`, `collection[id]` is `undefined`, and reading `.title` from it would throw an error.

Update the return statement to use a conditional. Return `artifact.title` if an artifact is found, and the string `"Artifact not found"` if it is not.

hints.text: `getArtifactTitle(101)` should still return `"Golden Mask"`.
`getArtifactTitle` should return `"Artifact not found"` if no artifact matches the `id`.
`getArtifactTitle` should return the title of any artifact it finds, not only `101`.

items.title: Step 8
items.description: The front desk needs to know which artifact is filed under `102`. Call `getArtifactTitle(102)` inside `console.log()` to log the returned title.

hints.text: You should call `getArtifactTitle(102)` inside `console.log()`.

items.title: Step 9
items.description:
Curators tag artifacts to make them easier to search, and a tag should never be added twice. Before adding a new tag, you can use the `includes()` method to check if it already exists, as it returns `true` when an array already contains a value.

Create a function named `addTag` that takes `id` and `tag` parameters. Look up the artifact using `collection[id]`. If it exists and its `tags` array does not already include `tag`, push `tag` onto `artifact.tags`.

hints.text: You should have a function named `addTag` with parameters named `id` and `tag`.
Calling `addTag` with a new tag should add that tag to the artifact's `tags` array.
Calling `addTag` with a tag the artifact already has should not add a duplicate.
`addTag` should add the tag to whichever artifact the `id` refers to.
`addTag` should not throw an error or change the collection when no artifact matches the `id`.
You should push `tag` onto the artifact's existing `tags` array, rather than replacing the array.

items.title: Step 10
items.description: New research confirms the Golden Mask belonged to royalty. Add the tag `"royal"` to the artifact with an `id` of `101`. Then, call `console.log()` with `collection[101].tags` to log that artifact's tags.

hints.text: You should call `addTag` with `101` and `"royal"`.
You should log the first artifact's `tags` to the console.
You should log the `tags` after adding the new tag.
The first artifact's `tags` should include `"royal"`.

items.title: Step 11
items.description:
As artifacts move between galleries over time, each move is recorded as a new entry in the `locations` array.

Create a `moveArtifact` function with the parameters `id`, `gallery`, and `year`. Find the artifact using `collection[id]`. If it exists, push a new object with the `gallery` and `year` to its `locations` array.

hints.text: You should have a function named `moveArtifact` with parameters named `id`, `gallery`, and `year`.
Calling `moveArtifact` should push a new `{ gallery, year }` object onto the artifact's `locations` array.
`moveArtifact` should push the new location onto whichever artifact the `id` refers to.
`moveArtifact` should not throw an error or change the collection when no artifact matches the `id`.
You should push the new location onto the artifact's existing `locations` array, rather than replacing the array.

items.title: Step 12
items.description: Move the artifact with the `id` `102` to `"Hall B"` in the year `2026`. Then, call `console.log()` with `collection[102].locations` to log that artifact's locations array.

hints.text: You should call `moveArtifact` with `102`, `"Hall B"`, and `2026`.
You should log the second artifact's `locations` to the console.
You should log the `locations` after moving the artifact.
The second artifact's most recent location should be `{ gallery: "Hall B", year: 2026 }`.

items.title: Step 13
items.description:
Over time, artifacts frequently go on and off display.

Create a `toggleDisplayStatus` function that takes an `id` parameter. Look up the artifact using `collection[id]`. If it exists, set its `onDisplay` property to the opposite of its current value.

hints.text: You should have a function named `toggleDisplayStatus` with a parameter named `id`.
Calling `toggleDisplayStatus` should flip the artifact's `onDisplay` value in both directions.
`toggleDisplayStatus` should not throw an error or change the collection when no artifact matches the `id`.

items.title: Step 14
items.description: Verify that your toggle works. First, call `console.log()` with `collection[102].onDisplay`. Next, call `toggleDisplayStatus(102)`. Finally, call `console.log()` with `collection[102].onDisplay` again.

hints.text: You should call `toggleDisplayStatus` with `102`.
You should log the second artifact's `onDisplay` value, then call `toggleDisplayStatus`, then log it again.

items.title: Step 15
items.description:
As your museum grows, the person responsible for an artifact can change.

Create an `updateCurator` function that takes `id` and `name` as parameters. Look up the artifact using `collection[id]`. If it exists, update the `name` property of its `curator` object to the provided `name`.

hints.text: You should have a function named `updateCurator` with parameters named `id` and `name`.
Calling `updateCurator` should change the `name` of the artifact's `curator` object.
`updateCurator` should change the curator of whichever artifact the `id` refers to.
`updateCurator` should not throw an error or change the collection when no artifact matches the `id`.

items.title: Step 16
items.description: Update the curator for artifact `101` to `"Fran Sinclair"`. Then, call `console.log()` with `collection[101].curator.name` to log that artifact's curator name.

hints.text: You should call `updateCurator` with `101` and `"Fran Sinclair"`.
You should log the first artifact's curator `name` again, after updating it.
The first artifact's curator `name` should be `"Fran Sinclair"`.

items.title: Step 17
items.description:
Finally, build a readable summary for any artifact. Start by handling the case where an artifact is missing.

Create a `buildSummary` function that takes an `id` parameter. Use `collection[id]` to look up the artifact, and store it in a variable named `artifact`. If the artifact is not found, return the string `"Artifact not found"`.

hints.text: You should have a function named `buildSummary` with a parameter named `id`.
You should assign `collection[id]` to a variable named `artifact`.
`buildSummary` should return `"Artifact not found"` when no artifact matches the `id`.
`buildSummary` should not return `"Artifact not found"` when the artifact exists.
hints.test:
assert.notStrictEqual(buildSummary(101), "Artifact not found");
assert.notStrictEqual(buildSummary(102), "Artifact not found");

items.title: Step 18
items.description:
An artifact's current gallery is its most recent location. You can find this by checking the last item in its `locations` array.

Declare a `currentLocation` variable and assign it `artifact.locations[artifact.locations.length - 1]`. This expression uses the array's `length` property to access its last element.

hints.text: You should declare a variable named `currentLocation` inside `buildSummary`.
You should assign the last element of the artifact's `locations` array to `currentLocation`.

items.title: Step 19
items.description:
Next, return a template literal summarizing the artifact. Put the title on the first line, followed by one line each for the category, curator's name, current gallery, and display status. Use `currentLocation.gallery` for the gallery.

For example, if you call `buildSummary(101)`, it should return:

```md
Golden Mask
Category: Ceremonial
Curator: Fran Sinclair
Current Gallery: Hall C
On Display: true
```

hints.text: `buildSummary(101)` should include the artifact's title, `Golden Mask`.
`buildSummary(101)` should include a `Category: Ceremonial` line.
`buildSummary(101)` should include a `Curator: Fran Sinclair` line.
`buildSummary(101)` should include a `Current Gallery: Hall C` line, using `currentLocation.gallery`.
`buildSummary(101)` should include an `On Display: true` line.
`buildSummary(101)` should put each field on its own line.
`buildSummary(102)` should use the most recent location, showing `Current Gallery: Hall B`.
`buildSummary` should build the summary from any artifact's own values, one field per line and in order.

items.title: Step 20
items.description:
Call `buildSummary(101)` inside `console.log()` to log the returned summary.

Congratulations! You have successfully completed the Artifact Provenance Auditor workshop.

hints.text: You should call `buildSummary(101)` inside `console.log()`.
